questions.question: A dealer sells two machines at Rs. 12000 each. On one it gains 32% and on the other it loses 32%. What is its profit/loss percentage in the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of one article be Rs. y and other be Rs. z

From the given problem statement, 32% gain can be given as

⇒ y × (1 + 32/100) = 12000

⇒ y = 12000/1.32

⇒ y = Rs. 9090.9

32% loss can be written as

⇒ z × (1 – 32/100) = 12000

⇒ z = 12000/.68

⇒ z = 17647.05

⇒ Total cost price = 9090.9 + 17646.05 = Rs. 26736.95

⇒ Total selling price = 12000 + 12000 = Rs. 24000

⇒ Loss = 26736.95 – 24000 = Rs. 2736.95

⇒ Loss percent = loss × 100/CP = 2736.95 × 100/26736.95

⇒ Loss percent = 10.24%

∴ Loss percent is 10.24%

ABCD is an isoceles trapezium such that AD||BC, AB = 5 cm, AD = 8 cm and BC = 14 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of trapezium?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4635cf3fba622c376a7ad9bfa61a79e44665892e276c4b5e131e0af6723d957.png] 

From the above figure Using Pythagoras theorem in triangle AOB

⇒ AB² = BO² + OA²

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (height) × (sum of parallel sides)

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 4 × (8 + 14) = 44

∴ The area is 44 cm²

questions.question: Amit can complete a work in 25 days and Punit can complete the same work in 20 days. Punit alone worked at it for 10 days and then left the work. In how many days will Amit alone complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Let the number of days required by Amit alone to do remaining work be y day’s

Work done by Amit in 1 day is 1/25th of the total work

work done by Punit in 1 day is 1/20th of the total work

According to the problem statement

⇒ 10 × (1/20) + y × (1/25) = 1

⇒ y = 25/2 = 12½

∴ 12½ days are required by Amit to do remaining work

questions.question: The measure of the four successive angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 7 : 11 : 7 : 11. The quadrilateral is a ______.

questions.question: If (x/y) + (y/x) = 1, then what is the value of x³ + y³?
questions.solution:
It can be simplified as x² + y² = xy

⇒ x² + y² – xy = 0 …(i)

And we know that x³ + y³ = (x + y)( x² + y² - xy), From (i)

⇒ x³ + y³ = 0

∴ x³ + y³ = 0

questions.question: If sec (3x – 20)° = cosec (3y + 20)°, what is the value of tan (x + y)?
questions.solution:
Since we know that sec(x) = cosec (90 - x), From the given equation

⇒ sec (3x – 20) = sec{90 – (3y + 20)} comparing the terms in brackets on LHS and RHS

⇒ 3x - 20 = 90 – (3y + 20)

⇒ x + y = 30

∴ tan(x + y) = tan(30) = 1/√3

questions.question: The average age of a class of 6 girls is x years. Four new girls having ages x – 2, x + 2, x + 4 and x + 6 joins the class. What is the new average age (in years) of the class?
questions.solution:
Before adding four new girls, average can be given as

⇒ Sum of age of 6 girls/6 = x

⇒ Sum of age of 6 girls = 6x

After adding age of 4 new girls average can be given as

⇒ New average = Sum of age of 6 girls + x – 2 + x + 2 + x + 4 + x + 6 /(6 + 4)

⇒ New average = (10x + 10)/10

⇒ New average = x + 1

∴ new average is x + 1

questions.question: A fraction becomes 6/5 when 5 is added to its numerator and becomes 1/2 when 4 is added to its denominator. What will be the value of the fraction?
questions.solution:
Let the fraction be a/b, From the questions statement

⇒ (a­ + 5)/b = 6/5

⇒ (5a + 25)/6 = b… (i)

When 4 is added to its denominator

⇒ a/(b + 4) = 1/2

⇒ 2a = b + 4 Using (i)

⇒ 2a = (5a + 25)/6 + 4

⇒ 7a = 49

⇒ a = 7 Put this in (i)

⇒ b = (5 × 7 + 25)/6

⇒ b = 10

∴ the fraction is 7/10

questions.question: How much water (in litres) must be added to 80 litres solution of milk and water containing 10% milk, so that it becomes a 5% milk solution?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since only water is added, the quantity of milk remains constant.

Milk in initial mixture = 10% of 80 L = 8 L.

In the new mixture, 5% of Total Volume = 8 L.

⇒ Total Volume = (8 × 100) ÷ 5 = 160 L.

Water added = Final Volume − Initial Volume = 160 L − 80 L = 80 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 80 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial quantity of mixture = 80 litres

Percentage of milk in initial mixture = 10%

Target percentage of milk = 5%

**Concept Used:**

We apply the alligation method on the concentration of milk. Pure water added contains 0% milk.

 Initial Mixture
 Added Water
 
 10%
 0%
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 5%
 
 5 - 0 = 5
 10 - 5 = 5
 
 Ratio = 5 : 5 = 1 : 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of Initial Mixture Quantity to Added Water Quantity = (5 − 0) : (10 − 5)

⇒ Ratio = 5 : 5 = 1 : 1

⇒ 80 / Added Water = 1 / 1

⇒ Added Water = 80 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 80 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

When two ingredients are mixed, the ratio of their quantities is inversely proportional to the differences of their concentrations from the mean concentration.

Constant Quantity Concept

In mixture problems where only one component is added or removed, the quantity of the other unadulterated component remains strictly constant throughout the process.

Successive Replacement

If V is the initial volume of pure liquid, and x volume is replaced by another liquid n times, the final amount of pure liquid left = V × (1 − x/V)ⁿ.

questions.question: A bus travels 2/5 of a total journey at its usual speed. The remaining distance was covered by bus at 6/7 of its usual speed. Due to slow speed it reaches its destination 50 minutes late. If the total distance is 200 kms, then what is the usual speed (in km/hr) of bus?
questions.solution:
Let its usual speed be a km/hr.

From the questions statement 2/5th of total journey is 2 × 200/5 = 80 km

⇒ 80/a + 120/(6a/7) – 200/a = 50/60

⇒ 80 + 140 – 200 = 5a/6

⇒ a = 24

∴ its usual speed is 24 km/hr

If a + b + c = 9 and ab + bc + ca = 18, then what is the value of a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc ?
questions.solution:
Since we know that a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² - ab - bc - ca)

And (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca Using the given data

⇒ 9² = a² + b² + c² + 2(18)

⇒ a² + b² + c² = 45 Put all these things in the required expression

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² - ab - bc - ca)

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc = 9 × (45 - 18) = 9 × 27 = 243

∴ a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc = 243

questions.question:
In the given figure, ABC is an equilateral triangle. If the area of bigger circle is 1386 cm², then what is the value of four times the area (in cm²) of smaller circle if the distance left between vertex A and point m on smaller circle can be assumed to be equal to the radius of small circle?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24a1e3b1c5fcd536edc7ef0346207004223f1e18332487043c1e506f49b3229c.png]
questions.solution:
Area of bigger circle = πr²

⇒ Area of bigger circle = πr² = 1386

⇒ Radius of the bigger circle = 21 cm

We know that the radius of the inscribed circle in the equilateral triangle is 1/3rd times the altitude of that triangle.

Altitude of the equilateral triangle = 3 × 21 = 63 cm

Let radius of the smaller circle be x.

3x + (2 × 21) = 63

x = 7 cm

⇒ Four times of area of smaller circle = 4 × π × (7)² = 4 × 154 = 616 cm²

questions.question: For an amount, simple interest at the rate of interest of 12% per annum for 6 years is Rs. 25920. What will be the compound interest (in Rs) on same amount at the rate of interest of 8% per annum compounding annually for 2 years?
questions.solution:
Let the amount be Rs. p

From the problem’s statement:

S.I = (p × r × t)/100

⇒ 25920 = (p × 12 × 6)/100

⇒ p = (25920 × 100)/(72)

⇒ p = 36000

Compound interest can be given as

⇒ CI = p((1 + 8/100)² - 1)

⇒ CI = 36000 × (1.08² - 1)

⇒ CI = 5990.4

∴ The CI is Rs. 5990.4

questions.question: Rs. 60500 is divided among A, B and C such that A receives 2/9 as much as B and C together and B receives 3/7 of as much as A and C together. What is the share of C (in Rs)?
questions.solution:
Let A, B and C’s share be a, b and c respectively

From the problems statement

⇒ a = 2 × (b + c)/9 …(i) and

⇒ b = 3 × (a + c)/7….(ii)

given that total amount to be distributed is Rs. 60500

⇒ a + b + c = 60500 …(iii)

Put (i) in (ii)

⇒ b = 3 × ((2 × (b + c)/9) + c)/7

⇒ b = (2b + 11c)/21

⇒ 19b/11 = c …(iv) 

put (i) and (iv) in (iii)

⇒ 2 × (b + 19b/11)/9 + b + 19b/11 = 60500

⇒ b = 60500 × 99/330

⇒ b = 18150 Put this in (iv)

⇒ c = 19 × 18150/11

⇒ c = 31350

∴ C’s share is Rs. 31350

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

a = 2 × (b + c)/9

⇒ (b + c) = 9a/2 ----(i)

b = 3 × (a + c)/7

⇒ (a + c) = 7b/3 ….(ii)

a + b + c = 60500 ----(A)

Putting equation i in the A

⇒ 9a/2 + a = 60500

⇒ a = 11000

Putting equation ii in the A

⇒ 7b/3 + b = 60500

⇒ b = 18150

Subtract 60500 with a and b value

⇒ c = 60500 - 11000 - 18150 

⇒ 31350

**∴ C’s share is Rs. 31350**

questions.question: If all the 3 categories increase by same rate in 2013 over 2012 as they did in 2012 over 2011, then what will be the total approximate sales (in ‘000 units) of all the 3 categories taken together in year 2013 ?
questions.solution:
Percentage increase in the sale of Hatchback over year 2011 is given as

⇒ (sale in next year – sale in previous year) × 100/(sale in previous year)

⇒ (800 - 650) × 100/650

⇒ 23.07% increase

⇒ Sale of hatchback in year 2013 can be given as

⇒ 800 × (1 + 23.07/100)

⇒ 984.6

Percentage increase in the sale of Sedan over year 2011 is given as

⇒ (sale in next year – sale in previous year) × 100/(sale in previous year)

⇒ (625 - 575) × 100/575

⇒ 8.69% increase

⇒ Sale of sedan in year 2013 can be given as

⇒ 625 × (1 + 8.69/100)

⇒ 679.34

Percentage increase in the sale of SUV over year 2011 is given as

⇒ (sale in next year – sale in previous year) × 100/(sale in previous year)

⇒ (750 - 400) × 100/400

⇒ 87.5% increase

⇒ Sale of hatchback in year 2013 can be given as

⇒ 750 × (1 + 87.5/100)

⇒ 1406.25

⇒ Total sale = 984.6 + 679.34 + 1406.25 = 3069 (approximately)

∴ the total sale is approximately 3069

questions.question: If cot A = n/(n + 1) and cot B = 1/(2n + 1), what is the value of cot (A + B)?
questions.solution:
Given cot A = n/(n + 1) and cot B = 1/(2n + 1) and we know that

cot (A + B) = (cotA cotB - 1) / (cotA + cotB), Putting all values in this

⇒ cot(A + B) = [{1/(2n + 1)} × {n/(n + 1)} - 1] / [{1/(2n + 1) + n/(n + 1)]

⇒ cot(A + B) = [{n – (2n + 1)(n + 1)} / {(2n + 1)(n + 1)}] / [{(n + 1) + n(2n + 1)} / {(2n + 1)(n + 1)}]

⇒ cot (A + B) = -1

∴ the value of cot(A + B) = -1

questions.question: What is the discount percentage offered on a book having marked price Rs. 2150 being sold at Rs. 1892?
questions.solution:
Discount can be calculated as (marked price – selling price) × 100/(marked price)

⇒ Discount = (2150 – 1892) × 100/ 2150

⇒ Discount = 12%

∴ The discount is 12%
